items.title: Tirzepatide in Adolescents With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Information on the effects of tirzepatide, a once-weekly glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist approved for obesity management in adults with obesity, remains limited in adolescents.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly tirzepatide in adolescents with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This phase 3, randomized, double-blind, 72-week clinical trial was conducted at 31 medical research centers and hospitals in Canada, the Czech Republic, Israel, Italy, Poland, and the US from October 16, 2023, to June 2, 2026, among adolescents aged 12 years to younger than 18 years with obesity or overweight with at least 1 obesity-related complication.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide, escalated to a maximum tolerated dose (5, 10, or 15 mg), or placebo for 72 weeks, in addition to healthy lifestyle intervention.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was percent change in body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) from baseline to week 72. Key secondary end points included percentages of participants achieving BMI reductions of at least 5%, at least 10%, at least 15%, and at least 20%; changes in BMI SD score; BMI expressed as a percentage of the 95th percentile; and body weight, waist circumference, and physical functioning from baseline to week 72. Safety outcomes included treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, and discontinuations due to adverse events.
RESULTS: A total of 160 participants were randomized to receive tirzepatide (n = 109) or placebo (n = 51). Mean (SD) age at baseline was 14.6 (1.6) years, 99 participants (61.9%) were female, mean body weight was 109.7 kg, and mean BMI was 38.6. At week 72, tirzepatide was associated with 18.5% reduction in BMI, compared with 0.5% increase in BMI with placebo, demonstrating superiority over placebo (estimated treatment difference, -19.0 [95% CI, -23.9 to -14.1] percentage points; P < .001). Of 10 key secondary outcomes, all demonstrated statistically significant differences favoring tirzepatide compared with placebo. Overall, 79.6% of tirzepatide-treated participants achieved BMI reduction of at least 5% compared with 28.5% of participants in the placebo group (risk difference, 51.2 [95% CI, 36.3-66.1] percentage points; P < .001). The most common adverse events with tirzepatide treatment were gastrointestinal (mostly mild to moderate).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In adolescents with obesity or overweight with obesity-related complications, tirzepatide, in addition to healthy lifestyle intervention, led to significant reductions in percent change in BMI compared with placebo at 72 weeks.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06075667.

items.title: Efficacy and safety of co-administered cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) 1·7 mg each and 1·0 mg each in adults with overweight or obesity (REDEFINE 9): a multicentre, randomised, double-blind within-dose-level, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3b trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cagrilintide-semaglutide (CagriSema) 2·4 mg each has shown clinically meaningful bodyweight reductions in global phase 3 studies. Different dosing options might support individual treatment responses and tolerability. We aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of once per week subcutaneous cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each or 1·0 mg each versus placebo in participants with obesity or overweight and at least one obesity-related complication.
METHODS: This multicentre, randomised, double-blind within-dose-level, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 3b trial (REDEFINE 9) was conducted across 24 sites in Canada, France, Germany, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older; with a BMI of at least 30 kg/m2 or at least 27 kg/m2 and one or more obesity-related complication; and without diabetes. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1:2:1) centrally, using block randomisation (block size of six) and a web-based system, to receive cagrilintide 1·7 mg plus semaglutide 1·7 mg (hereafter cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, starting at 0·25 mg each and escalated over 12 weeks), placebo 1·7 mg plus 1·7 mg (hereafter placebo 1·7 mg each), cagrilintide 1·0 mg plus semaglutide 1·0 mg (hereafter cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, starting at 0·25 mg each and escalated over 8 weeks), or placebo 1·0 mg plus 1·0 mg (hereafter placebo 1·0 mg each) for 68 weeks, plus nutrition and physical activity counselling until week 74. All treatments were administered subcutaneously once per week. The coprimary endpoints were relative mean change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68 and proportion of participants reaching a bodyweight reduction of at least 5% at week 68, assessed in the full analysis set (defined as all randomly assigned participants). Safety was assessed in the safety analysis set (defined as all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose of the study drug). This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06388187 (completed).
FINDINGS: From June 24 to Oct 30, 2024, 333 participants were assessed for eligibility and 24 were excluded. 309 participants were randomly assigned (full analysis set: 104 assigned to cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, 103 to cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and 102 to pooled placebo). 308 participants received at least one dose of the study drug. 291 (94%) of 309 participants completed the study and 254 (82%) were on treatment at week 68. The mean age was 48·0 years (SD 13·6) and mean BMI was 39·1 kg/m2 (6·8). 239 (77%) participants were female, and 70 (23%) were male. For the efficacy estimand, the mean relative change from baseline in bodyweight at week 68 was -20·7% (SE 0·9) with cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, -21·0% (1·0) with cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and -2·0% (1·0) with the pooled placebo. Bodyweight reductions were significantly greater with both doses of cagrilintide-semaglutide than with placebo (estimated treatment difference [ETD] -18·8 percentage points [95% CI -21·5 to -16·0]; p<0·0001 for the 1·7 mg each dose and -19·0 percentage points [-21·8 to -16·2]; p<0·0001 for the 1·0 mg each dose). The proportion of participants reaching bodyweight reductions of at least 5% at week 68 was significantly greater with cagrilintide-semaglutide than with placebo (95·1% [SE 2·7] with the 1·7 mg each dose vs 33·4% [5·6] with placebo, ETD 61·7 percentage points [95% CI 49·5-74·0], p<0·0001; and 96·3% [2·2] with the 1·0 mg each dose, ETD 63·0 percentage points [51·1-74·9], p<0·0001). Adverse events were reported in 102 (99%) of 103 participants receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·7 mg each, 98 (95%) of 103 receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide 1·0 mg each, and 93 (91%) of 102 receiving the placebo. Most adverse events were mild or moderate and gastrointestinal-related. No deaths were reported.
INTERPRETATION: Cagrilintide-semaglutide at 1·7 mg each and 1·0 mg each was superior to placebo at reducing bodyweight in adults with overweight or obesity, suggesting that different dose levels might support treatment flexibility.

items.title: Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized to receive once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide (target doses of 2 mg, 4 mg, or 6 mg) or matching placebo for 48 weeks, with dose escalation for up to 20 weeks and concomitant lifestyle intervention.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was change in body weight from baseline to week 48, including percent change in body weight and the percentage of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction, analyzed under the treatment policy estimand.
RESULTS: Among 567 randomized participants (309 [54.5%] female; mean [SD] age was 34.4 [8.4] years, body weight was 93.0 [17.3] kg, and body mass index was 33.3 [4.5]), 514 (90.7%) completed the 48-week treatment period. Least-squares mean percentage changes in body weight at week 48 were -10.7%, -16.4%, and -17.7% with ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg, respectively, vs -1.4% with placebo. At week 48, the placebo-adjusted differences in percentage change in body weight were -9.3 (95% CI, -11.4 to -7.3) percentage points with ribupatide 2 mg, -15.0 (95% CI, -17.1 to -12.9) percentage points with ribupatide 4 mg, and -16.3 (95% CI, -18.4 to -14.2) percentage points with ribupatide 6 mg (P < .001 for all). For at least 5% body weight reduction at week 48, the multiply imputed response rates were 68.1% (95% CI, 59.9% to 75.3%) for ribupatide 2 mg (97 of 142), 88.0% (95% CI, 81.3% to 92.6%) for ribupatide 4 mg (124 of 141), 85.7% (95% CI, 78.6% to 90.7%) with ribupatide 6 mg (121 of 141), and 16.0% (95% CI, 10.8% to 23.1%) with placebo (23 of 143). Placebo-adjusted differences for ribupatide 2, 4, and 6 mg were 52.0 (95% CI, 42.2 to 61.9), 72.0 (95% CI, 63.7 to 80.2), and 69.7 (95% CI, 61.1 to 78.3) percentage points, respectively (all P < .001). The most frequent treatment-emergent adverse events with ribupatide were gastrointestinal events, occurring in 47.9%, 58.2%, and 63.1% of participants receiving ribupatide 2 mg, 4 mg, and 6 mg, respectively, compared with 23.1% receiving placebo; most were mild to moderate in severity and few participants (0.7%) permanently discontinued study treatment because of adverse events.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes, once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide resulted in significantly greater weight loss at 48 weeks. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most frequent tolerability findings.

items.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Childhood obesity is a chronic, neurometabolic disease with limited options for medical treatments that are efficacious and durable. Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide is approved for the treatment of obesity in adolescents and adults, but data for its use in young children are lacking.
METHODS: We conducted a phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide or placebo for a period of 104 weeks, after which participants stopped taking semaglutide or placebo for a 7-week washout period. Both groups received counseling for lifestyle modification. The primary end point was the percent change in the body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) from baseline to week 68. The confirmatory secondary end point was a reduction in BMI category at week 68.
RESULTS: Among 167 children who underwent randomization, 112 were assigned to receive semaglutide and 55 to receive placebo. At week 68, the mean percent change in BMI was -13.5% with semaglutide and 2.7% with placebo (estimated between-group difference, -16.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -19.4 to -12.9; P<0.001). The percent change in BMI at week 104 was -9.4% with semaglutide and 8.4% with placebo (between-group difference, -17.8 percentage points; 95% CI, -22.2 to -13.3). At week 68, a reduction in BMI category had occurred in 79% of the participants in the semaglutide group and in 23% of those in the placebo group (odds ratio, 7.8; 95% CI, 3.5 to 17.6; P<0.001), with the BMI below the threshold for obesity (the 95th percentile for age and sex) in 38% of the participants who received semaglutide and in 2% of those who received placebo. Adverse events occurred in 96% of the participants receiving semaglutide and in 93% of those receiving placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were the most common, occurred more frequently with semaglutide than with placebo, and led to discontinuation in 1 participant in the semaglutide group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among children (6 to <12 years of age) with obesity, treatment with semaglutide for 68 weeks resulted in a significantly greater mean percent reduction in BMI than placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; STEP Young ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05726227.).

items.title: Cannabidiol for Severe Behavioral Problems in Youths With Intellectual Disability: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: There is a high level of interest in cannabidiol (CBD) as treatment for severe behavioral problems in children with intellectual disabilities. Given the lack of evidence, clinical trials are needed to inform practice.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy of CBD to reduce severe behavioral problems in children and adolescents with intellectual disability.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This parallel design, double-blind placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial was conducted between May 11, 2021, and May 8, 2025. Participants were children and adolescents aged 6 to 18 years with an intellectual disability and severe behavioral problems from 3 children's hospitals in Australia: The Royal Children's Hospital in Melbourne, Monash Children's Hospital in Melbourne, and The Children's Hospital Westmead in Sydney.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to receive CBD isolate in oil (10 mg/kg/d) or placebo orally for 8 weeks, with a 4-week follow-up period.
MAIN OUTCOME AND MEASURE: The primary outcome was parent-reported score on the Aberrant Behavior Checklist, Irritability (ABC-I) subscale assessed at the end of the 8-week maintenance phase.
RESULTS: Of 131 participants randomized after exclusion of 1 participant randomized in error, 65 were in the CBD group and 66 were in the placebo group. Overall, mean (SD) age was 11.2 (3.1) years, and 98 participants (74.8%) were male. A total of 110 participants (84.0%) had comorbid autism. Primary outcome data were available for 61 participants in the CBD group and 63 in the placebo group. Mean (SD) ABC-I subscale scores at baseline were 32.2 (7.3) and 30.0 (6.3) in the CBD and placebo groups, respectively. Intention-to-treat analysis showed similar mean (SD) ABC-I subscale scores at the end of treatment: 21.7 (11.0) in the CBD group and 19.2 (10.7) in the placebo group (mean difference, 2.4; 95% CI, -1.5 to 6.3). A similar proportion of participants experienced at least 1 adverse event in the CBD group (41 [63.1%]) and the placebo group (40 [60.6%]).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial, CBD was not effective in treating severe behavioral problems in youths with intellectual disability. The results suggest that CBD should not be used to treat severe behavioral problems in this population.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04821856.

items.title: Targeting F.nucleatum with metronidazole plus tislelizumab and fruquintinib in MSS colorectal cancer: A multicenter phase 2 study.
items.abstract: Fusobacterium nucleatum has been linked to chemoresistance and immune evasion in colorectal cancer (CRC), but therapeutic strategies targeting this bacterium remain limited. In this multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 trial (NCT06356597), 33 patients with Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive, microsatellite-stable metastatic CRC received the combination treatment of tislelizumab, fruquintinib, and the antimicrobial metronidazole. The primary endpoint was met, with a median progression-free survival of 6.0 months. The objective response rate and disease control rate were 19.4% and 83.9%, respectively. Grade 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 30.3% of patients, with no grade 4 or 5 events. Metagenomic analysis showed that metronidazole reduced Fusobacterium nucleatum abundance. Exploratory analyses associated clinical benefit with enrichment of Lactobacillus species and nonresponse with Enterococcus. Fecal microbiota transplantation from responders sensitized germ-free mice to the treatment, which enhanced cytotoxic CD8+ T cell differentiation and reduced terminal exhaustion. These findings support further evaluation of this combination in Fusobacterium nucleatum-positive metastatic CRC.

items.title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial.
items.abstract: Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01E-adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one (n = 131) or two doses 30-60 days apart (n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years (n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

items.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Accommodations, Behavior Therapy, and Stimulant Medication: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Although widely deployed, little is known about the efficacy of academic accommodations for attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), alone or in combination of behavior therapy and stimulant medication.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy of academic accommodations alone and in combination with behavioral interventions and stimulant medication.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a crossover randomized clinical trial with participants introduced to all conditions. Children with ADHD were enrolled in kindergarten through sixth grade. Academic accommodations were changed daily in a randomized order. Stimulant medication and placebo alternated weekly. The general classroom and enhanced behavior classroom intervention alternated every 2 weeks. The study was conducted in summer treatment program classrooms. For the present study, behavior was evaluated in (1) a classroom period where participants completed independent assignments and (2) a classroom period where participants were taught a lesson, completed small group cooperative tasks related to the lesson, and then took a quiz. Study data were analyzed from March to July 2026.
INTERVENTIONS: The single and combined effects of academic accommodations, behavior therapy, and stimulant medication (methylphenidate, 0.3 mg/kg) were evaluated. Academic accommodations were extended time on tasks, frequent breaks during tasks, a low-distraction workspace, and the ability to stand at the desk, compared with a condition without an accommodation. A general classroom setting was compared with a classroom setting with enhanced behavior intervention.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Main outcomes were classroom rule violations during each of the two, 1-hour class periods, the number of seatwork items completed correctly (ie, academic productivity), and the quiz score.
RESULTS: Of 306 children screened, 280 were enrolled in the study. A total of 255 children (mean [SD] age, 8.8 [1.6] months; 201 male [79%]) started the intervention, and 235 (84%) completed the study. Compared with placebo, stimulant medication increased effects related to seatwork productivity by 22% (ie, the rate ratio [RR] for this condition indicated that receiving medication compared with placebo multiplied the expected count of problems completed per minute by 1.22; 95% CI, 1.19-1.25), and quiz scores were significantly improved by 3.9 points (95% CI, 3.10-4.70 points). Medication and behavioral therapy significantly reduced classroom rule-breaking behavior by 37% (RR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.60-0.67) and 61% (RR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.37-0.42), respectively. There was no evidence that any of the academic accommodations significantly improved behavior or academic outcomes. No interactions were significant.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this crossover randomized clinical trial question whether school-based academic accommodations for children with ADHD should continue to be emphasized as accommodations were ineffective when used alone or in combination with other ADHD treatments. Results support the continued use of behavioral and pharmacological treatment for ADHD.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05469386.

items.title: Acupoint Thread Embedding for Weight Loss in Women With Overweight or Obesity : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether acupoint thread embedding (ATE), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention, produces weight reduction remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of ATE for weight reduction in women with overweight or obesity.
DESIGN: Randomized, sham-controlled trial masked to participants, outcome assessors, and analysts. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06316310).
SETTING: Acupuncture Department, Shanghai Municipal Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.
PARTICIPANTS: 132 women aged 18 to 45 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 24.0 kg/m2 or greater.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to ATE (6 sessions over 12 weeks) or sham ATE (superficial needle insertion at the same acupoints without manipulation, de qi, thread placement, or needle retention), followed by a 12-week follow-up.
MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was change in BMI from baseline to week 12, analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: At week 12, BMI and body weight decreased 0.7 kg/m2 (95% CI, -1.0 to -0.3 kg/m2) and 1.8 kg (CI, -2.7 to -0.9 kg), respectively, more with ATE than with sham ATE; at week 24, differences were -1.1 kg/m2 (CI, -1.7 to -0.6 kg/m2) and -3.0 kg (CI, -4.5 to -1.6 kg), respectively. Weight reduction of 5% or more occurred in 25.8% versus 9.1% (risk difference, 16.7 percentage points [CI, 3.7 to 29.3 percentage points]) at 12 weeks. Acupoint thread embedding produced greater reductions in waist and hip circumference, body fat percentage, and appetite scores, whereas cardiometabolic and patient-reported outcomes did not differ. Adverse events were mild and comparably distributed.
LIMITATION: Single center, generally healthy women of reproductive age, unmasked acupuncturists, short-term follow-up, and underpowered for uncommon adverse events and subgroup analyses.
CONCLUSION: Acupoint thread embedding produced modest but sustained reductions in BMI and adiposity-related measures in Chinese women of reproductive age with overweight or obesity.
PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Facility for Translational Medicine (Shanghai).

items.title: Effect of intensive blood pressure control on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes: prespecified analysis of secondary outcomes of BPROAD randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of intensive compared with standard treatment of systolic blood pressure (SBP) on cognitive outcomes and brain structures in adults with type 2 diabetes.
DESIGN: Multicentre, open label, outcome assessor masked, randomised controlled trial.
SETTING: 145 clinical centres across seven geographical regions in China.
PARTICIPANTS: 12 821 adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes, raised SBP, and increased cardiovascular risk, of whom 12 434 without probable dementia at baseline were included in this cognitive ancillary study. Further assessments were performed annually and at the end of study.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned to receive intensive treatment targeting SBP <120 mm Hg or standard treatment targeting SBP <140 mm Hg for up to five years.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary cognitive outcome was a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment. Secondary cognitive outcomes included all cause dementia, mild cognitive impairment, changes in cognitive functions, and changes in brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) characteristics. A subset of participants underwent brain MRI at baseline (n=862) and at the end of study (n=605) to assess changes in white matter lesion volume and total brain volume.
RESULTS: 6219 participants were assigned to receive intensive treatment and 6215 to receive standard treatment. Baseline mean age was 63.7 years, and 5567 (44.8%) participants were women. After one year, mean SBP was 121.6 mm Hg in the intensive treatment group and 133.2 mm Hg in the standard treatment group. During a median follow-up of 3.8 years, the primary cognitive outcome of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment occurred in 747 participants (3.69 events per 100 person years) in the intensive treatment group and 783 participants (3.89 events per 100 person years) in the standard treatment group (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.86 to 1.06; P=0.38). In the MRI substudy (428 intensive treatment v 434 standard treatment), the intensive treatment group had a smaller increase in white matter lesion volume compared with the standard treatment group (between group difference -0.09 inverse hyperbolic sine (asinh) transformed cm3, 95% CI -0.15 to -0.02; P=0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Over a median of about four years, no statistically significant difference in incidence of a composite of all cause dementia or mild cognitive impairment was observed among adults with type 2 diabetes receiving standard treatment of SBP (target <140 mm Hg) and intensive treatment (target <120 mm Hg). Intensive treatment was, however, associated with a reduction in the accrual of cerebral white matter lesion volume.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03808311.

items.title: Absolute Risk of Progression to Cognitive Impairment Based on Plasma Phosphorylated Tau 217, Age, Sex, and APOE ε4.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Alzheimer disease (AD) pathology can be detected years before symptom onset, but some individuals who are biomarker positive and cognitively unimpaired (CU) remain asymptomatic.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate 5- and 10-year absolute risks of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia using continuous plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) and p-tau217/amyloid β 42 (Aβ42).
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study included participants from the Mayo Clinic Study of Aging (MCSA) and the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). Participants were CU individuals aged 60 to 90 years with baseline Fujirebio Lumipulse plasma p-tau217 measurements, APOE genotyping, and longitudinal clinical follow-up. The MCSA is a population-based longitudinal cohort of residents in Olmsted County, Minnesota; ADNI is a multicenter observational cohort. MCSA data were ascertained from October 2008 to September 2025; ADNI data from September 2005 to January 2026.
EXPOSURES: Age, sex, APOE ε4, p-tau217, and p-tau217/Aβ42.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Transition from CU to MCI and dementia estimated using continuous-time multistate models.
RESULTS: In the MCSA cohort (n = 1644), the median (IQR) age was 72 (66-79) years; 804 participants (49%) were female and 840 (51%) were male. In the ADNI cohort (n = 534), the median (IQR) age was 72 (68-77) years; 297 participants (56%) were female and 237 (44%) were male. A p-tau217 of 0.324 pg/mL vs 0.072 pg/mL (90th vs 10th percentile) was associated with 2.66 (95% CI, 2.02-3.51), 3.02 (95% CI, 2.21-4.12), 2.62 (95% CI, 1.99-3.46), and 2.79 (95% CI, 2.04-3.81) greater hazard of clinical progression in MCSA female participants who did not carry the APOE ε4 variant (ε4-), females who did carry the APOE ε4 variant (ε4+), males who were ε4-, and males who were ε4+, respectively. In ADNI, hazards were 2.67 (95% CI, 1.86-3.85), 2.83 (95% CI, 1.89-4.22), 2.08 (95% CI, 1.48-2.92), and 3.99 (95% CI, 2.59-6.13), respectively. In MCSA, higher baseline p-tau217 and older age were associated with greater absolute risk of progression. At age 75 years and assuming sex and APOE are at the MCSA means of 0.511 and 0.268, 5-year absolute risk of MCI increased from 7% (95% CI, 5%-8%) to 17% (95% CI, 13%-20%) for a p-tau217 concentration of 0.072 vs 0.324 pg/mL; 10-year absolute risk of MCI increased from 15% (95% CI, 12%-18%) to 35% (95% CI, 29%-41%; P < .001 for both). At 0.324 pg/mL, 5-year MCI risk increased from 6% (95% CI, 4%-8%) to 37% (95% CI, 32%-43%) for ages 65 to 85 years; 10-year risks were 17% (95% CI, 12%-21%) and 66% (95% CI, 57%-74%; P < .001 for both). Results were similar for p-tau217/Aβ42.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that higher plasma p-tau217 and older age were associated with higher 5- and 10-year risk of cognitive impairment. Plasma p-tau217 concentrations, combined with age, sex, and APOE ε4 status, can enable individualized estimation of short-term absolute risk of cognitive impairment in CU individuals, with applications in prognosis and trial enrichment in preclinical AD.

items.title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery.
items.abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer's blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

items.title: Genome-directed treatment targets and mutational signature biomarkers: a retrospective, pan-solid tumour analysis.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical application of precision oncology therapies is currently restricted to selected cancer cases harbouring highly specific mutations. Targeted therapies are typically approved for use in specific tumour types in which these alterations occur frequently. We aimed to systematically catalogue targetable alterations and genome-wide biomarkers across all solid tumour types to identify additional therapeutic opportunities.
METHODS: In this retrospective, pan-solid tumour analysis, for the primary cancer cohort, we used matched fresh frozen tumour and normal DNA samples and anonymised patient metadata from a discovery cohort of 11 013 tumours comprising 19 tumour types collected from 10 334 participants in the UK-based 100 000 Genomes Project (100kGP). Participants were recruited to this cohort through 13 National Health Service Genomic Medicine Centres or hospitals affiliated to the 100kGP between 2012 and 2019. For the metastatic cancer cohort, we used matched tumour and normal DNA samples and anonymised patient metadata from a cohort of 6016 solid tumours collected from 5658 patients from the Netherlands who contributed to the Hartwig Medical Foundation (HMF) database (accessed Aug 19, 2025). Snap-frozen tumour DNA and matched normal DNA from blood samples underwent whole-genome sequencing. Potentially targetable alterations, comprising (1) immediately actionable alterations, (2) investigational alterations, and (3) mutational signature-informed features, were sought in all samples. The primary outcome of this study was to assess the pan-cancer frequency and tissue distribution of potentially targetable alterations.
FINDINGS: Between July 1, 2025, and March 3, 2026, we analysed samples from 17 029 tumours from the 100kGP and HMF cohorts. Immediately actionable alterations were identified in 2081 (18·9%) of 11 013 primary and 1559 (25·9%) of 6016 metastatic cancers; a further 1204 (10·9%) primary and 867 (14·4%) metastatic cancers harboured investigational alterations or mutational signature-informed features. 2914 (51·1%) of the 5706 immediately actionable variants identified were found in tumour types where the biomarker is not approved by the US Food and Drug Administration. Although some immediately actionable alterations (including gene-fusion targets and MET exon 14 skipping variants) were restricted to fewer tumour types, most immediately actionable alterations (including HER2 amplification, RAS-RAF pathway alterations, IDH1 mutations, and DNA repair deficiencies) occurred across multiple tumour types, frequently beyond those for which matched targeted therapies are currently approved. Mutational-signature biomarkers of DNA repair or replication deficiencies were similarly observed across tumour types. Metastatic cancers, including rare and moderately rare tumour types and cancers of unknown primary, harboured a notably high prevalence and diversity of targetable events.
INTERPRETATION: Our findings support comprehensive whole-genome sequencing assessment of cancers irrespective of tumour type. Prospective clinical trials are required to establish whether therapeutic vulnerabilities identified by whole-genome sequencing can extend the effective use of targeted therapies beyond their current tumour-specific indications.
